extracted.intended_audience: general readers, television fans, and media researchers interested in Conan O'Brien and late-night talk-show formats
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the format, production, and variants of the Conan late-night talk show (2010–2021), including its hour- and half-hour structures, sketches, guest selection, production practices, and special episodes. Useful for producing or analyzing a comedy/variety talk show in a similar style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode structure (six-piece late-night format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan initially followed the established six-piece late-night format popularized by evening talk show hosts such as Johnny Carson and David Letterman. Each episode of Conan from its first eight years runs 60 minutes in length, including commercials, and typically consists of: Act 1: Monologue; Act 2: Comedy Bit(s); Act 3: Celebrity Interview 1; Act 4: Celebrity Interview 1 continued; Act 5: Celebrity Interview 2; Act 6: Musical or Stand-Up Comedy Guest, Signoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This canonical segmentation defines pacing and where material types belong (news-driven monologue up front, bits following, interviews in middle acts, musical/stand-up closing). It anchors decisions about time allocation and flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening titles / sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The original hour-long show opened with Richter proclaiming "Coming to you from Warner Bros. Studios in Burbank, it's Conan!", introducing O'Brien, The Basic Cable Band, and the episode's guests. For the first several seasons, each episode had a title, which Richter would announce at the end of the opening sequence; the titles were in the style of old-fashioned murder-mystery radio shows, television sitcoms, or other assorted jokes. The episode titles were dropped in early 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opening sequences can establish tone and branding; Conan's used playful episode titles and graphic design inspired by Saul Bass. Variations and periodic redesigns are acceptable to refresh the show's image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monologue content and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: O'Brien opened each episode with a monologue drawing from current news stories and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monologues may be accompanied by clips and brief comedy skits and include interactions between host, sidekick, and audience. Reliance on recent news anchors topicality; use of multimedia/interaction enhances variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketches and comedy bits (placement and variety)
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more comedy bits followed the monologue. Some comedy bits (such as those based on video clips) were presented from the monologue stage; following the first commercial break, additional comedy sketches were typically presented from the desk area. Some sketches were original and appeared only once. Occasionally an additional sketch would air between the first and second guest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketches can be staged from different locations on set depending on format; mix of recurring and one-off bits provides variety. Placement relative to commercial breaks affects audience retention and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest selection and variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests for the show came from a wide range of cultural sources, and included actors, musicians, authors, athletes and political figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A varied guest list (celebrities, cultural figures, athletes, political figures) broadens appeal. The article gives examples (e.g., Tom Hanks as first guest in the half-hour relaunch) and notes cameos and unusual choices, including fan-influenced choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running time and format change
rubrics_metrics.description: The hour-long show ran 60 minutes (2010–2018). Starting January 22, 2019, the show was reformatted to a half-hour length (2019–2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running time determines allowable segments, depth of interviews, and pacing. Format changes (hour → half-hour) require rethinking segment structure and priorities (e.g., fewer interviews, more focused comedy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Half-hour format features (2019–2021)
rubrics_metrics.description: The new half-hour format would not feature a band or a desk area, and for the first time as host of a talk show, O'Brien would not be wearing a suit. The relaunch promised a looser structure with fewer celebrity interviews and more comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing band/desk and tightening the set shifts emphasis to faster, more flexible segments and a more casual host presentation. These are explicit design choices to alter tone and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production adaptability (pandemic response and remote production)
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the program switched to a remotely-produced format from O'Brien's home beginning March 30, 2020. In July 2020 the show continued with limited on-site staff from the Coronet Theatre in Los Angeles and no studio audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows must be able to adapt production methods (remote production, limited crew, no audience) while preserving content. The page notes Conan was among the first late-night shows to film outside the host's residence during the pandemic period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episodes on location and special tapings
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan taped episodes on location at venues like the Beacon Theatre (NYC), Chicago Theatre, Tabernacle (Atlanta), Majestic Theatre (Dallas), Spreckels Theatre (San Diego/Comic-Con), Apollo Theater (Harlem) and others for festivals and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Location episodes are tied to events (festivals, Comic-Con, sports tournaments) and can feature tailored guest lists and sketches. On-location tapings may bring back house band or special guest collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conan Without Borders — international special format
rubrics_metrics.description: These episodes do not follow the traditional talk-show format, instead following O'Brien as he attempts to engage the locals and experience the unique cultural aspects of the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International specials emphasize cultural engagement and documentary-style segments rather than standard desk interviews. These specials can win awards and achieve high popularity (e.g., an Emmy win in 2018) and be distributed on streaming platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set design and staging choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Set designers adopted a 'theatre' appearance with warm wood tones and electric blue screens; the new set featured items like a remote-controlled moon and an ocean backdrop transformed for effect. In 2018 a new set depicted a studio backlot; in 2019 the half-hour set was more compact and intimate (armchairs around a coffee table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set design is used deliberately to establish tone (intimate vs. theatrical), alter host-entry points, and facilitate segment logistics. Changing sets can reflect format changes and desired audience relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: House band and theme music
rubrics_metrics.description: Jimmy Vivino and the Basic Cable Band served as the house band from 2010 until the end of the hour-long format in 2018. The new theme song was co-written by Vivino and O'Brien. A smaller band returned for the final two weeks of Conan in 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence or absence of a band (and theme composition) affects musical transitions, tone, and the show's live feel. Band leadership and musical identity are part of branding and can change with format shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards, critical reception and editorial reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The show received nominations and awards (e.g., Emmy nominations and wins, Outstanding Variety Talk Series nomination in 2021). Early reviews described it as a "looser, quirkier" late-night show and provided mixed critical reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and critical reviews are used as external measures of quality and cultural impact. The article lists multiple Emmy-related nominations/wins and excerpts from critics as indicators of reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratings, viewership trends, and audience demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite a promising start (4.1 million viewers at premiere), Conan suffered low viewership throughout its run and declining Nielsen ratings; however, it boasted strong online revenues and a particularly young viewership, with online videos attracting billions of views. Surveys suggested Conan drew more Hispanic viewers and performed well among low-income inner-city viewers in some rankings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linear TV ratings are a traditional success metric, but online engagement and demographic profiles (young audience, online video views) are increasingly important for evaluating modern talk-show performance and advertiser value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production schedule and rehearsal practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Taping of each episode began at 4:30 p.m. PST, which usually followed a rehearsal lasting from 1 p.m. until 3 p.m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consistent rehearsal and taping schedule supports timely production, coordination of sketches, band, and guest logistics. Documented schedules inform staffing and technical planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and content positioning (edginess and audience targeting)
rubrics_metrics.description: O'Brien and Richter indicated the new show's effort not to reuse previous sketches and signaled it would more closely represent Late Night than Tonight in regard to content and material, implying edgier or questionable content excised for an earlier time slot would no longer be an issue at TBS. O'Brien said he was 'no longer interested in 'broadening' the audience or trying to reach everybody of all ages,' implying content would not be toned-down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about target audience and acceptable edginess shape writing choices, sketch content, and guest booking. Network/time-slot constraints influence how far material can push boundaries; cable can allow different freedoms than broadcast.
